task: Give every chunk of a multi-page document a stable identity so all chunks of a SharePoint file survive retrieval deduplication instead of collapsing into one.

component_scope.label: L
component_scope.affected: BaseDatasourceProcessor (shared abstract base subclassed by 7 connectors), RRF reciprocal-rank-fusion deduplication
component_scope.layers: Datasource/Indexing, Service (search and rerank), persisted Elasticsearch chunk-metadata contract

requirements_clarity.label: M
requirements_clarity.gaps: The outcome (all chunks retrievable) was unambiguous, but two definitional questions were left open at implementation time and only surfaced in review: what constitutes chunk identity for a compound file whose documents share one source but carry different file_path values, and what the counter's lifetime is across reused processor instances. Both are now pinned down by comments in _split_documents and _next_chunk_num and by dedicated tests.

technical_risk.label: L
technical_risk.risk_factors: Change lands in shared code on the hot path of every knowledge base: BaseDatasourceProcessor._split_documents runs for all 7 connectors, and RRF._filter_duplicates runs on every retrieval. No exact precedent existed for chunk numbering that spans loader batch boundaries. Already-indexed documents carry no chunk_num and cannot be migrated, so the dedup key must stay correct for two data generations simultaneously. Failure mode is silent: wrong identity drops chunks from results rather than raising. Counter is per-instance mutable state, so its reset lifecycle is load-bearing. Review empirically confirmed the risk: 2 blocking findings (chunk-identity collision for compound files, untested reset path).
technical_risk.mitigation: Legacy documents without chunk_num fall back to the Elasticsearch document id as the dedup key, so no reindex or migration is required. Identity is keyed on SOURCE rather than document_key, and chunk_num is re-applied after _process_chunk so metadata-stripping subclasses cannot drop it. Behaviour is pinned by tests covering cross-batch numbering, compound files, per-run reset, metadata-stripping subclasses, legacy chunks and genuine duplicates.

affected_layers.label: M
layers_changed: Data persistence (Elasticsearch chunk-metadata contract, no migration)

key_reasoning.reason: Only 2 production files, but both are shared: BaseDatasourceProcessor is the abstract base that all 7 connectors subclass, and RRF sits on every retrieval path. Blast radius, not line count, sets this score.

New approach with no precedent (numbering that survives batch boundaries), a silent failure mode, and a backward-compatibility constraint from unmigratable indexed data. One review round produced 2 blocking findings, confirming the risk was real rather than theoretical.
5 files modified, 0 new, across 5 directories — but 272 of the 283 inserted lines are tests; net production change is 11 lines.

Indexing writes chunk identity, retrieval reads it, and the two are coupled through the persisted Elasticsearch document shape. No migration was written; the legacy fallback absorbs the older data generation instead.
No manifest touched — no new packages, no version changes, no config additions.

red_flags_applied: Component Scope bumped from M (3) to L (4): touches core shared utilities — BaseDatasourceProcessor is subclassed by 7 connectors and RRF deduplication runs on every retrieval.
